correctness.rationale: Exact log-odds conjugacy yields H(s)=s+a(b-sigma(s)). The embedded Python rational interval program covers each of the two rational width-0.004 seed intervals and every real parameter in the strict rectangle. Integer outward grid arithmetic with a rigorously bounded exponential Taylor tail certifies fourth-return derivative suprema below 0.51 and 0.72, with center residuals below 0.00095 and 0.00053. Both are less than the corresponding (1-k)*0.002 margins, so H^4 is a contraction mapping each interval strictly into itself. Exact H^2-disjointness and four-phase cross-disjointness prove primitive period 4 and distinctness; negative Schwarzian and two critical points, with repelling endpoints, give the previously published upper bound of two attracting cycles. The checker executes successfully. No claim is made about all repelling cycles.

value.rationale: The published maximal-bistability region had been supported by numerical bifurcation plots. It is mathematically meaningful to certify that the sharp two-attractor upper bound is actually attained by two geometrically distinct primitive four-cycles on an explicitly quantified open two-parameter set. This rules out floating-point cycle misidentification and proves robustness for every real parameter there; exact finite-dimensional witness is valuable even without optimizing the region or producing a global census.
